title: The Multilingual Alignment Prism: Aligning Global and Local Preferences to Reduce Harm

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to human-annotated red-teaming prompts categorized as either 'global' (universally recognized harms) or 'local' (nuanced harms specific to a particular culture or region), measuring harmful generation rates using LLM-as-a-judge to assess alignment with diverse cultural preferences.

Comparing safety performance (percentage of harmful generations) and general-purpose capabilities (win-rates on Multilingual Dolly-200 and FLORES-200) across six different languages (English, French, Spanish, Hindi, Russian, Arabic) to assess cross-lingual transfer and performance disparities in non-English settings.

bias_targets.target: Demographic and Identity bias (including Race, Gender, Religion, Sexual Orientation)
bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the model with the custom Aya Red-teaming dataset, which explicitly includes categories for 'Discrimination & Injustice', 'Hate Speech', and 'Harms of Representation Allocation' targeting protected attributes, and measuring the rate of harmful or prejudicial text generated.
